name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
summary: A compound free-weight pulling exercise performed in a hinged position to strengthen the back and hip stabilizers.

setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart and mid-foot directly beneath a loaded barbell.
Hinge at the hips with a slight bend in the knees, maintaining a neutral spine until your torso is roughly 45 degrees to nearly parallel to the floor.
Grasp the bar with a double-overhand (pronated) grip slightly wider than shoulder width, letting the arms hang fully extended.
steps: Brace your core and pull your shoulder blades back as you drive your elbows toward the ceiling.
Pull the barbell smoothly toward your lower ribcage or upper abdomen, keeping your elbows close to your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the stroke for a brief contraction.
Lower the barbell under control until your arms are fully extended and your scapulae protracted, keeping your torso angle fixed.
instructions.breathing: Inhale and brace your abdomen before initiating the pull; exhale as you complete the row or lower the weight under control.
cues: Drive your elbows back and up.
Keep your chest proud and spine rigid.
Pull to your belly button, not your neck.

common_faults.fault: Using excessive body momentum or standing up during each repetition.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load and lock your torso angle in place throughout the entire set.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lumbar spine under load.
common_faults.correction: Hinge at the hips, brace your core, and maintain a flat, neutral spine before initiating the row.
Tuck the elbows roughly 30 to 45 degrees from the sides to bias the lats and protect the shoulders.

precautions: Avoid letting the spine flex under heavy loads; set the bar down if posture breaks down.
